question: Why do residual connections make very deep neural networks easier to train?
short_answer: They create identity shortcuts, so blocks learn residual changes and gradients have shorter paths through the network.
expanded_answer: A plain stack must learn the entire desired mapping. A residual block instead learns F(x) while an identity path carries x directly, producing F(x) + x. This makes an identity-like solution easy and improves forward and backward signal propagation, reducing the optimization degradation seen in very deep plain networks.
key_points: The block learns a residual rather than the full mapping.
Identity shortcuts provide short paths for signals and gradients.
ResNet addresses optimization degradation, not merely classic overfitting.
common_misconceptions: Skip connections do not guarantee gradients are numerically unchanged; they provide an additional direct path.
